keyVerseText: There came also a multitude out of the cities round about unto Jerusalem, bringing sick folks, and them which were vexed with unclean spirits: and they were healed every one.
rootMeaning: The word πέριξ (périx) is an adverb derived from the preposition περί (perí), which conveys the idea of 'around' or 'about.' This root emphasizes a sense of surrounding or encircling something completely. Unlike the simple English phrase 'round about,' the Greek root carries a nuanced spatial sense of encompassing or being circumjacent, indicating something that is not merely near but fully encircling or encompassing in all directions.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, πέριξ appears only once, translated as 'round about' in Acts 5:16. This singular occurrence shows the word consistently conveys the idea of surrounding areas or regions adjacent to a central place, in this case, cities encircling Jerusalem. Its use as an adverb highlights the spatial relationship of proximity and completeness, emphasizing the all-encompassing nature of the surrounding regions involved in the narrative.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding πέριξ enriches our grasp of how Scripture communicates God's reach and the spread of His healing power. The notion of 'round about' underscores the inclusiveness of divine grace extending beyond a central location to encompass all neighboring areas, reflecting the expansive nature of the Gospel. This spatial fullness mirrors the comprehensive scope of Christ’s ministry and the early church’s mission to reach all people, not just a select few. Recognizing the original meaning helps believers appreciate the all-encompassing, boundary-crossing work of God in the world.
keyVerseReflection: Acts 5:16 records that a multitude came from the cities 'round about' Jerusalem, bringing the sick and those troubled by unclean spirits to be healed. The term πέριξ here highlights the surrounding regions actively engaging with the central place of ministry, demonstrating how the healing power of God through the apostles was not confined to Jerusalem alone but was accessible to all nearby communities. This word enriches the verse by portraying a dynamic movement of faith and healing that transcends geographic boundaries.
